(5 July) | attendance = 3,189,482{{cite web|url=https://data.j-league.or.jp/SFTP01/?startPage=0&endPage=5&competitionFrameId=2&prev_next=&nextBtnVal=1&prevBtnVal=0|title=2023明治安田生命J2リーグ|access-date=12 September 2023|language=ja|website=data.j-league.or.jp}} | average attendance = 6,904 | prevseason = [[2022 J2 League|2022]] | nextseason = [[2024 J2 League|2024]] | updated = }} The '''2023 J2 League''', also known as the {{Nihongo|'''2023 [[Meiji Yasuda Life|Meiji Yasuda]] [[J2 League]]'''|2023 明治安田生命J2リーグ|2023 Meiji Yasuda Seimei J2 Rīgu|lead=yes}} for sponsorship reasons, was the 25th season of the [[J2 League]], the second-tier Japanese professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1999. ==Overview== This was the last season to be played with 22 participating clubs, as the number of clubs was reduced to 20 from the 2024 season.{{cite news |title=League Structure and Competition Format from 2024 Season Unify the number of clubs in each category to 20 League Cup changed to a knockout competition with participation of all J1, J2 and J3 clubs |url=https://aboutj.jleague.jp/corporate/en/release/league-structure-and-competition-format-from-2024-season-unify-the-number-of-clubs-in-each-category-to-20-league-cup-changed-to-a-knockout-competition-with-participation-of-all-j1-j2-and-j3-clubs/ |access-date=9 February 2023 |publisher=Japan Professional Football League |date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222103628/https://aboutj.jleague.jp/corporate/en/release/league-structure-and-competition-format-from-2024-season-unify-the-number-of-clubs-in-each-category-to-20-league-cup-changed-to-a-knockout-competition-with-participation-of-all-j1-j2-and-j3-clubs/ |archive-date=22 December 2022 |url-status=dead}} [[FC Ryukyu]] and [[Iwate Grulla Morioka]] were relegated to the [[2023 J3 League]], finishing the previous [[2022 J2 League|J2 League]] season as 21st and 22nd-placed team, respectively. Relegated from [[2022 J1 League|J1]], both [[Shimizu S-Pulse]] and [[Júbilo Iwata]] were the only [[Shizuoka Prefecture|Shizuoka-based]] J1 teams last season. Now, they return to J2 after spending six and one season, respectively, at the top flight. [[2022 J3 League|J3]] winners [[Iwaki FC]] and runners-up [[Fujieda MYFC]] were both promoted from the [[J3 League]]. Both teams make their debut in [[J2 League]], with Iwaki being promoted to the J2 just a season after being promoted to J3. For the first time ever since the [[2004 J.League Division 2|2004 season]], three teams from the same prefecture participate in the J2 League, as [[Shimizu S-Pulse]], Júbilo Iwata and Fujieda MYFC are all based on [[Shizuoka Prefecture]]. ==Participating clubs==

Promotion play-offs, officially called the ''2023 J.League Road To J1 Play-offs'' ({{langx|ja|2023 J1昇格プレーオフ}}), was held from the semi-finals, where the match-ups were previously semi-determined. Based on the J2 placements at the end of the regular season, the third-placed team played against the sixth-placed, while the fourth-placed team played against the fifth-placed. The winners of the semi-finals played the final, with the winners promoted to the J1. If a match was tied in the play-offs, the team with the higher rank won. The rank order was: J2's third, fourth, fifth, and sixth-placed teams.{{cite web|url=https://www.jleague.jp/news/article/26435/|website=JLeague.jp|publisher=Japan Professional Football
